title: RWB-S8-E7003-APP: the X3 branch has no plan row for its four consumed contracts, its rule read, its outbox and its workflow, and no source names the claim reference, the heir notification or the escalation level
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R5.7, R7.3 and R9; split plan slices RWB-S8-E7003-APP and RWB-S8-E7003-CON; context pack S8 rwb-deviation (service row, ownership rows, Architecture v5 slides 3, 4, 5, 8 and 13, Temporal and Drools slides 5, 8 and 13); legacy RWB-E7-003; FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A1.4, A2.12 and Requirements served; TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 T2, T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T3.3, T4, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1 and T-A; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-22; Event and Messaging Design v4, EV-06 and EV-07; API Specification v4, Deviation, DeviationRequest and DeviationOutcome
description: (1) The plan gives H = RWB-S8-E7003-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON with C, I and X empty, while the branch reads the rwb-source-data customer, the rwb-case case and timers, the rwb-access authorise row and the rwb-decision rule package and claim approval, so four consumed rows have no plan row. (2) DP-04 is absent although the branch evaluates the DEV route set of 22 rules over 9 states. (3) DP-09 is absent although the service owns EV-06 and EV-07 and the branch publishes EV-06 through an outbox. (4) DP-10 is absent although the ownership rows give S8 one workflow, DeviationWorkflow, and the branch runs five activities on task queue rwb-deviation. (5) The connection matrix shows no REST edge from S8 to P7, while FSD A2.12 names the rules component in the path and R-DEV-06 needs the approval of an insurance claim, so the rule read and the approval carry a placeholder. (6) No source names a column, a table or a list for the insurance claim reference, the heir notification reference or the escalation level: deviation carries outcome, LOV-DEV-OUTCOME and no claim or notification field, and the 10-working-day level is a BRD and rule-row value. (7) R-DEV-06 is published for X6 and X7 in TSD S8 T4 and in the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, while the legacy AC3 of this key pairs R-DEV-06 with X3 and the FSD A2.12.3.1 repeats it. (8) The legacy Data table names recovery_case, assignment, timer, v_ace_customer and document, none of which this service may read or write, and the legacy endpoints carry the monolith base. (9) The split plan carries no requirement id for this slice.
evidence: split plan slices RWB-S8-E7003-APP and RWB-S8-E7003-CON with three H rows and empty C, I and X; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04, DP-05, DP-09 and DP-10 rows; context pack S8 ownership rows (table deviation, 2 REST operations, events EV-06 and EV-07, no job, workflow DeviationWorkflow) and connection-matrix row S8 (E to P3, R E to P1, T E to P10); TSD S8 T4 rule table (R-DEV-06 condition deviation_code in (X6,X7)); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-22; FSD S8 A2.12.3.1 and A2.12.3.3; Event and Messaging Design v4, EV-06 and EV-07; TSD S8 T-A.2 error sets without message ids; legacy RWB-E7-003 Data, Endpoints, Acceptance criteria and Guardrails
area: Dependency, ownership, data and requirement trace
proposed: Keep the plan's H, C, I and X rows as they stand and record the rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision rows as class C in fact with their placeholders; record the embedded rule read, the outbox and inbox library RWB-PLT-TE006-CON and the workflow kit RWB-PLT-E1071-CON as tracked dependencies; settle the S8-to-P7 edge with the connection matrix owner and republish the slide or the placeholder; decide with the data owner whether deviation gains a claim-reference and a notification-reference column before the DB story, and keep the escalation level in the rule row; settle R-DEV-06's code list with the rule owner so that X3 and the AC agree; adopt REQ-DVH-008 and REQ-S8-001 for traceability

title: RWB-S8-E7003-CON: the consumed operation names, the case event name, the target event names, the claim approval and the lists of values of rwb-deviation have no published baseline
source: Template and Rules v1 R4, R5.4, R5.5, R7.2 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S8-E7003-CON; context pack S8 rwb-deviation; legacy RWB-E7-003; FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.12.2 and A2.12.3.1; TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 T2, T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1, T6.2 and T-A.1 and T-A.2; API Specification v4, Deviation, DeviationRequest and DeviationOutcome; Event and Messaging Design v4, EV-06 and EV-07
description: (1) The rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision rows name no operation, so four consumed rows carry a placeholder. (2) No source publishes the case event that opens or resumes a stage, so the one subscription carries a placeholder and no topic path. (3) No catalogue publishes the target names of EV-06 and EV-07; only the naming rule of Template and Rules R4 gives their form, and the baseline derives rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1 and rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1 from it. (4) No source publishes the operation or the workflow that approves an insurance claim, although AC3 and R-DEV-06 require a person's approval before the claim is filed; the approval is declared as a row of rwb-decision with a placeholder. (5) TSD S8 T3.2 publishes three lists of values and no list for the deviation state machine, so the nine DEVIATION states are referenced as the rows of T4 and no list identifier is declared for them. (6) TSD S8 T-A.2 gives error sets as status codes with no message ID per condition, so each condition is bound to a message of the legacy and FSD set. (7) T-A.2 publishes no required list for DeviationRequest and DeviationOutcome while API Specification v4 publishes one for Deviation, so the requiredness of the request is stated as copied. (8) The plan's C, I and X rows of this slice are empty while the baseline declares four consumed rows, one publication and one subscription.
evidence: TSD S8 T-A.1 operations API-S8-001 and API-S8-002, T-A.2 error lists of 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 without message ids, T3.1 field list, T3.2 three lists of values, T5.2 module interfaces with no operation name and T5.3 events; API Specification v4 required list of Deviation only; context pack ownership rows (table deviation, 2 REST operations, events EV-06 and EV-07, no job, workflow DeviationWorkflow); Event and Messaging Design v4, EV-06 payload caseId, deviationCode, raisedBy and consumers timers and communications; legacy RWB-E7-003 messages MSG-S8-001, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P7-003
area: Contract surface, interface names and vocabulary
proposed: Publish the baseline with the placeholders, bind every error condition to one message ID of section 14, confirm the four operation names, the case event name and the two event names with their owners before the tag, declare the claim approval as a row of rwb-decision and rate the S8-to-P7 edge, and record the tag date in the contract README
